structured_output.summary: The audit's core establishment is correct and independently verified: openCreatorCheckpointTrust() authenticates only pinned genesis plus one predecessor/current pair (creator-checkpoint.ts:246-307), the hard-cut/anchor schemas carry no per-author resolved sequence (creator-close.ts:64-80,387-410), DurableIssuanceStore exposes six methods with a watermark-free readLineage (types.ts:83-90), the pruning receipt is unsigned local maintenance state (maintenance.ts:14-43), no product path calls prunePublishedPrefix(), and the epoch-3 rejection of the genuine epoch-1 row is exactly v3-live.ts:4550-4624/5097-5098/7377-7439. The selected carrier is also sound in principle: the creator finality key is provably stable and genesis-pinned (creator-checkpoint.ts:252-276; creator-close.ts:538 forces nextSignerSet == current), the one-use protocol-owned signing request matches the existing keychain pattern exactly (finality.ts:136-157; seal-authority-custody.ts:145-162), the mint moment is non-circular (every binding — close graph, sealed replay, snapshot manifest, cut, commit QC, successor anchor — is already materialized at creator-close.ts:487-571, immediately before the closure is built at 572), and stale/forked/cross-room/cross-author replay is closed by binding the successor head to the independently authenticated room floor. Four blocking defects remain. (1) The frozen GREEN step 4 is not implementable within the declared owner set: @ts-drp/control-plane's closure-advance law admits no candidate other than the successor trust record plus two proof refs, and it gates close staging, adoption, cold reopen, and pending resume. (2) The mint rule refuses signing on any pending/non-member address above the prior boundary and has no representable "nothing resolved yet" value, so a reachable fresh room (unpublished pinned-genesis bootstrap row) cannot initialize and any close holding an unpublished outbox row cannot mint — which, under the frozen "each close requires exactly one previous checkpoint" rule, permanently blocks later closes and reopen. (3) An address pending at its own close can never satisfy the current-anchor/close-graph predicates afterwards, pinning the boundary below it forever and reproducing the exact demonstrated epoch-3 admission failure. (4) The boundary formula's exhausted branch yields Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER under the store's own invariant, taking an unbounded value straight from untrusted storage. RED is causal and feasible as specified and scope is otherwise well fenced, but the carrier design and owner set must be corrected before RED is authorized.

findings.title: GREEN step 4 is unimplementable: the closure-advance law admits no added or replaced candidate, and the omitted owner is @ts-drp/control-plane
findings.evidence: packages/control-plane/src/creator-trust-advance.ts:88-99,161-167 requires the proposed closure to equal exactly (current closure − current trust ref) + successor trust ref + the two proof refs (`combined.length !== input.proposed.closure.length` rejects any extra ref). packages/control-plane/src/creator-trust-checkpoint-advance.ts:205-215 does the same for epoch≥1: `retained.length !== typed.current.closure.length - 4`, then `expected = [...retained, proposed.trustRef, newCutRef, newQcRef]` compared with `exactClosure`. Any candidate that is not the trust record or a proof ref must be carried forward byte-identically; adding a new retirement ref and dropping the prior one is rejected as TRUST_CLOSURE_INVALID. packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:572-592 builds the proposed closure literally in that shape and validates it before stageCombinedGeneration. The same predicate gates three retained authenticators in verify mode: packages/node/src/creator-adoption.ts:358 (adoption), :1056 (cold reopen), :1390 (pending resume). Plan lines 95763-95766 and the owner sentence at 95778-95781 name only protocol-v3, keychain, creator-close capture, the node-internal transition classifier, and AHE closure preservation, and assert the design 'reuses ... exact AHE blob/ref storage, and current room-floor authority'.
findings.required_action: Add @ts-drp/control-plane's `inspectCreatorTrustAdvance` and `inspectBoundedCreatorTrustAdvance` (and their three verify-mode consumers at creator-adoption.ts:358, 1056, 1390) to the 0c1a owner list at line 95778-95781, and freeze the exact extended law: a proposed closure may additionally drop exactly the one prior retirement ref and add exactly one new retirement ref (zero prior refs only for the epoch-0 initialization), counted in both stage and verify modes, with retained gates proving every other closure delta still fails closed with the existing reasons.

findings.title: Mint rule refuses signing on any pending address and has no representable empty boundary, so a reachable fresh room can never initialize its checkpoint
findings.evidence: Lines 95730-95734 require every address above the prior boundary to have `published` state and make 'pending ... rows refuse signing', while GREEN item 3 (95804) says 'derive the dense published boundary' — the two are inconsistent. Unpublished rows across a close are a supported product state: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6082 rebases displaced rows only when `publishState === "pending"`. The pinned-genesis bootstrap row is hidden with no publish-state check at all (v3-live.ts:4593-4595 via authenticatedPinnedGenesisOutboxRow at 4515-4548), and the plan itself records this at 95521-95523 ('the current genesis filter's publish-state-blind treatment of an unpublished old row'), so a fresh room whose sequence-0 bootstrap row is unpublished at the 0→1 close has zero qualifying addresses. There is also no value to sign in that case: an absent lineage returns `{exhausted:false, next:0}` (packages/storage-node/src/internal/node-issuance-store.ts:275), so `lineage.next - 1` is -1, which `isValidDurableAuthorSequence` rejects (packages/issuance-store/src/contract.ts:141-143); line 95711 makes the new sequence non-nullable. Because 95721-95722 requires every later close to consume exactly one authenticated previous checkpoint, a close that cannot mint permanently blocks all later closes and reopen.
findings.required_action: Rewrite 95730-95734 so the new boundary is the longest verified dense published prefix strictly above the prior boundary — truncate at the first address that is missing, pending, or not a close-graph/replay member, and reserve refusal for a verification failure at or below the derived boundary — and make the new inclusive sequence explicitly nullable with a frozen 'none' value for a first checkpoint that covers zero addresses, restating that all addresses above the boundary keep offline/rebase custody.

findings.title: An address pending at its own close can never be certified later, pinning the boundary and reproducing the demonstrated epoch-3 failure
findings.evidence: Lines 95731-95733 require each newly covered address to bind the 'exact current room/anchor/epoch' and to be present in the captured close graph and sealed durable replay of the closing epoch. A row issued in epoch N but published only in epoch N+1 can satisfy neither predicate at the N+1→N+2 close: its vertex anchor is the epoch-N anchor and its digest is in the epoch-N close set. Combined with the dense-prefix requirement, that address pins the boundary below itself for the remaining life of the room, so at any later reopen it stays above the boundary and falls through to the existing current/displaced admission, which is exactly the rejection demonstrated at packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:5097-5098 and cited by the audit as the seam being closed. The state is reachable: v3-live.ts:6082 shows displaced rows still in `pending` publish state after a transition, and the retained D.110c-d gate requires 'offline/rebase outbox and first-successful-publication continuity' across close boundaries.
findings.required_action: State the disposition explicitly at 95731-95737: either prove in the plan that no address can remain unpublished across its own close on the product path (naming the owner that enforces it), or record that such addresses permanently pin the boundary, that D.110c-0c1 therefore still fails closed for them, and name the slice that owns their resolution — do not leave the carrier claiming an age-independent boundary it cannot advance.

findings.title: Boundary formula's exhausted branch yields Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER straight from untrusted storage
findings.evidence: The frozen derivation `lineage.exhausted ? lineage.next : lineage.next - 1` is evaluated against a store-supplied lineage, and the codebase invariant is that `exhausted === true` implies `next === Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`: packages/storage-node/src/internal/node-issuance-store.ts:283 rejects any other exhausted row, and the same rule is enforced at packages/issuance-store/src/terminal.ts:57, maintenance.ts:73, and conformance.ts:82. Under the plan's own untrusted-durable-bytes threat model (95516), a hostile or corrupt lineage row of `{exhausted:true, next:9007199254740991}` makes the scan range unbounded (2^53 addresses, no `maxEpochVertices` cap is stated for it) and makes the signed `throughAuthorSequence` — per the audit's wording at .logs/d110c-0c1-architecture-audit-d6f5de26/audit.md:79 — a value read directly from the database rather than derived from verified rows.
findings.required_action: Replace the exhausted branch at 95729 with an explicit fail-closed rule: when `lineage.exhausted` is true the mint refuses with the frozen token and signs nothing; otherwise the lineage supplies only a non-authoritative upper bound and the scan terminates at the last verified dense published address under the combined `maxEpochVertices` ceiling. Add one adversarial GREEN row asserting a store-supplied exhausted lineage produces exactly one refusal without an unbounded scan.

findings.title: Audit inventory omits the existing D.109d AHE pruning-receipt boundary, which D.110c-c must reconcile with the new signed boundary
findings.evidence: The 'Existing proof inventory' treats `prunedThroughAuthorSequence` only as store-local maintenance state, but packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:2825-2853 already enforces a per-author boundary latch in the live plane: `issuance.prunedThroughAuthorSequence === registration.displacedIssuanceBoundary` (2845) together with closedEpoch, issuance scope, snapshot-manifest digest, exactly one matching commit-QC ref inside `registration.payload.proposedClosure`, and the AHE active generation/expected head; the latch preimage is built at v3-live.ts:2856-2886. It is not age-independent (displacedIssuanceBoundary is derived at v3-live.ts:5078 from the immediate-predecessor scan), so the audit's conclusion and family selection stand, but this is the nearest existing per-author frontier and the future pruning consumer would see two competing boundaries.
findings.required_action: Disposition: record in the plan (near 95754-95759) that the existing D.109d receipt law `prunedThroughAuthorSequence === displacedIssuanceBoundary` at v3-live.ts:2845 is a named downstream reconciliation obligation for D.110c-c/D.110c-0c1, owned there and untouched by 0c1a.
